title: Leviticus Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who did the LORD call and speak to out of the tabernacle of the congregation?
options: Moses
Aaron
David
Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:1 states that the LORD called unto Moses and spake unto him out of the tabernacle of the congregation.

questions.question: To whom were the children of Israel commanded to bring their offerings?
options: To the priests
To the LORD
To the elders
To Moses
questions.correctAnswer: To the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:2 commands speaking unto the children of Israel that if any man brings an offering, it shall be brought unto the LORD.

questions.question: What kinds of animals are mentioned for offerings in Leviticus 1:2?
options: Fish and birds
Cattle, herd, and flock
Wild beasts and reptiles
Fowls and insects
questions.correctAnswer: Cattle, herd, and flock
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:2 mentions offerings of the cattle, even of the herd, and of the flock.

questions.question: What is required of the burnt sacrifice from the herd?
options: Any animal of the herd
A female without blemish
A male without blemish
Only a calf
questions.correctAnswer: A male without blemish
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:3 specifies that the burnt sacrifice of the herd must be a male without blemish.

questions.question: Where is the offering to be presented when offered voluntarily?
options: At the city gate
At the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
In the fields
At the altar of incense
questions.correctAnswer: At the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:3 says the offering shall be offered at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the LORD.

questions.question: What action must the offerer do with his hand upon the burnt offering?
options: Bless it
Put his hand upon the head
Anoint it with oil
Cut it into pieces
questions.correctAnswer: Put his hand upon the head
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:4 states he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering for atonement.

questions.question: What is the purpose of putting the hand upon the burnt offering's head?
options: To bless the offering
To accept it for atonement
To consecrate the animal
To designate it for sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: To accept it for atonement
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:4 explains that this act causes the offering to be accepted to make atonement for the offerer.

questions.question: Who kills the bullock before the LORD?
options: The priests
The offerer
The Levites
The elders
questions.correctAnswer: The offerer
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:5 says he shall kill the bullock before the LORD.

questions.question: Who brings the blood and sprinkles it upon the altar?
options: The offerer
Aaron's sons, the priests
The Levites
Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron's sons, the priests
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:5 states the priests, Aaron's sons, shall bring the blood and sprinkle it round about upon the altar.

questions.question: What must be done to the burnt offering after it is killed?
options: It must be anointed with oil
It must be flayed and cut into pieces
It must be washed with water
It must be buried
questions.correctAnswer: It must be flayed and cut into pieces
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:6 commands that the burnt offering shall be flayed and cut into pieces.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD spoke to Moses from the tabernacle of the congregation.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:1 states that the LORD called unto Moses and spake unto him out of the tabernacle of the congregation.

questions.question: True or False: The offering could be any animal from the flock, regardless of blemish.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:3 and 1:10 specify that the offering must be a male without blemish, showing blemish disqualifies the animal.

questions.question: True or False: The priests themselves kill the bullock before the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:5 says he (the offerer) shall kill the bullock before the LORD; the priests only bring and sprinkle the blood.

questions.question: True or False: The burnt offering is considered an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:9 and other verses describe the burnt sacrifice as an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD.

questions.question: In Leviticus 1, which instruction comes first?
options: Offer a male without blemish
Put hand upon the head of the burnt offering
Speak unto the children of Israel
Kill the bullock before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Speak unto the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:2 commands speaking unto the children of Israel before instructions about the offering are given in verses 3 and onward.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:7, what is the first action the sons of Aaron the priest must do before placing the wood on the altar?
options: Lay the wood in order upon the fire
Put fire upon the altar
Sprinkle blood on the altar
Kill the burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: Put fire upon the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:7 states that the sons of Aaron the priest shall first put fire upon the altar, and then lay the wood in order upon the fire. This shows the sequence of preparing the altar for the burnt offering.

questions.question: In Leviticus 1:8, which parts of the burnt offering do the priests place in order upon the wood on the altar?
options: The head and the legs
The fat and the legs
The parts, the head, and the fat
The inwards and the skin
questions.correctAnswer: The parts, the head, and the fat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:8 specifies that the priests, Aaron's sons, shall lay the parts, the head, and the fat in order upon the wood on the fire. This highlights the importance of these particular parts in the burnt offering.

questions.question: What must be done to the inwards and legs of the burnt offering according to Leviticus 1:9?
options: They must be burned on the altar
They must be eaten by the priests
They must be washed with water
They must be given to the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They must be washed with water
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:9 explains that the inwards and legs shall be washed in water before the priest burns all on the altar. This washing signifies purification before the sacrifice is completed.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:10, what kind of offering must be brought if it is from the flocks for a burnt sacrifice?
options: A female without blemish
A male without blemish
Any animal from the flock
A young animal with a blemish
questions.correctAnswer: A male without blemish
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:10 states that if the burnt offering is from the flocks, such as sheep or goats, it must be a male without blemish, emphasizing the need for a perfect offering.

questions.question: Where must the offering from the flocks be killed according to Leviticus 1:11?
options: On the south side of the altar
On the north side of the altar
Outside the camp
Inside the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: On the north side of the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:11 instructs that the offering shall be killed on the side of the altar northward before the LORD, showing the specific location for the sacrifice.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 1:12 describe the handling of the offering after it is killed?
options: It shall be eaten by the priests
It shall be cut into pieces with the head and fat and laid on the altar wood
It shall be buried outside the camp
It shall be given to the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be cut into pieces with the head and fat and laid on the altar wood
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:12 explains that the offering shall be cut into pieces, including the head and fat, and the priest shall lay them in order on the wood on the altar, showing the preparation for burning.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 1:8-9 teach us about the importance of order and cleanliness in worship?
options: Order and cleanliness are unnecessary in worship
Only the priests need to be clean, not the offerings
The priests lay parts of the offering in order and wash certain parts before burning, symbolizing reverence and purity
The offerings are handled carelessly to show humility
questions.correctAnswer: The priests lay parts of the offering in order and wash certain parts before burning, symbolizing reverence and purity
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 show the priests laying parts of the offering in order on the altar and washing the inwards and legs with water before burning, teaching the values of reverence and ritual cleanliness in worship.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 1:7-9 suggest about the role of the priests in the burnt offering process?
options: They only supervise but do not touch the offering
They prepare the altar fire, arrange the sacrifice parts, and burn the offering, mediating between God and the people
They kill the offering themselves
They eat the burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: They prepare the altar fire, arrange the sacrifice parts, and burn the offering, mediating between God and the people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:7-9 describes the priests putting fire on the altar, arranging the parts, and burning the offering, indicating their role as mediators performing sacred duties for the people.

questions.question: Based on Leviticus 1:10-12, what is the significance of bringing an offering without blemish?
options: It shows negligence in selection
It signifies giving God the best and reflects faith and obedience
It is to save money on animals
It is only a tradition without meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies giving God the best and reflects faith and obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 emphasize a male without blemish as the offering, teaching that worship requires integrity, faith, and giving God the best as an act of obedience.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 1:9-12 illustrate the connection between obedience to ritual and forgiveness?
options: By showing that proper sacrifice rituals lead to atonement and being accepted by God
By ignoring rituals and focusing on prayers
By emphasizing sacrifices only for priests
By focusing on offerings from other nations
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that proper sacrifice rituals lead to atonement and being accepted by God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:9-12 details the proper handling of offerings, which makes the burnt sacrifice a sweet savor to the LORD, symbolizing atonement and acceptance when done in obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 1:7-8, the priests are responsible for laying fire and arranging the burnt offering on the altar.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:7-8 clearly states that the sons of Aaron shall put fire on the altar and arrange the parts of the burnt offering, showing their responsibility in these tasks.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 1:10 commands that female animals without blemish may be offered as burnt sacrifices from the flock.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:10 specifies a male without blemish from the flock is required for burnt sacrifices, so female animals are not appropriate for this offering.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 1:11 describes the blood of the offering being sprinkled around the altar by the priests.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:11 states that the priests shall sprinkle the blood round about upon the altar, showing the ritual significance of the blood in the sacrifice.

questions.question: If a believer struggles with understanding the importance of giving their best to God, how does Leviticus 1:3 and 1:10 provide biblical guidance?
options: They show that offerings can be imperfect
They emphasize bringing a male without blemish as a voluntary act, teaching faith, integrity, and honoring God with the best
They allow for any animal to be offered
They suggest offerings are optional and unimportant
questions.correctAnswer: They emphasize bringing a male without blemish as a voluntary act, teaching faith, integrity, and honoring God with the best
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:3 and 1:10 instruct bringing a male without blemish voluntarily, which teaches believers to offer their best to God out of faith and obedience.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 1:8-9 promise will happen if the priests lay the parts, head, and fat in order upon the wood and wash the inwards and legs as instructed?
options: The offering will be rejected
The offering will be an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
The offering must be eaten by the priests
The offering will have no effect
questions.correctAnswer: The offering will be an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:8-9 explains that proper arrangement and washing lead to the burnt sacrifice being made by fire, producing a sweet smell to the LORD, symbolizing acceptance and atonement.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:13, what must be washed with water before the burnt offering is burned on the altar?
options: The inwards and the legs
The head and the fat
The horns and hooves
The wings and feathers
questions.correctAnswer: The inwards and the legs
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:13 states that the inwards and the legs shall be washed with water before the priest burns the entire offering on the altar.

questions.question: Leviticus 1:14 introduces burnt offerings of fowls. Which birds are specified for this offering?
options: Turtledoves or young pigeons
Sparrows or quails
Eagles or vultures
Cranes or storks
questions.correctAnswer: Turtledoves or young pigeons
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:14 specifically mentions turtledoves or young pigeons as the birds to be brought for burnt offerings to the LORD.

questions.question: In Leviticus 1:15, what action does the priest perform on the offering before burning it on the altar?
options: Wring off its head and wring out the blood at the side of the altar
Cut off its wings and sprinkle the blood on the altar
Remove its feathers and burn them separately
Slaughter it and offer the whole body uncut
questions.correctAnswer: Wring off its head and wring out the blood at the side of the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:15 explains that the priest shall wring off the bird's head and wring out its blood at the side of the altar before burning it on the altar.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:16, where is the crop and feathers of the burnt offering bird placed?
options: Beside the altar on the east part, by the place of the ashes
On the altar fire itself
In a separate holy vessel
Thrown into the river outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Beside the altar on the east part, by the place of the ashes
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:16 states the crop with its feathers is plucked away and cast beside the altar on the east part by the place of the ashes.

questions.question: Leviticus 1:17 instructs the priest to cleave the burnt offering bird with its wings but not divide it asunder. What is the significance of this action?
options: It symbolizes the completeness of the offering without dismemberment
It is a method to prepare the bird for cooking
It is a way to separate clean and unclean parts
It reflects a pagan ritual custom incorporated into Israelite worship
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the completeness of the offering without dismemberment
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:17 shows the offering must be cleft with the wings but not divided, emphasizing the offering's integrity and completeness as a burnt sacrifice.

questions.question: What is a recurring phrase in Leviticus 1:9, 1:13, and 1:17 describing the burnt offering?
options: An offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
A sacrifice once for all
A sin offering to remove guilt
A peace offering to the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: An offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
questions.explanation: These verses include the phrase 'an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD,' highlighting the burnt offering's purpose as pleasing to God through the aroma of sacrifice.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 1:10 states that the burnt offering from the flock must be a female without blemish.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:10 specifies the burnt offering from the flock must be a male without blemish, not female.

questions.question: How does the practice of placing the blood around the altar in Leviticus 1:5 and 1:11 foreshadow New Testament themes?
options: It prefigures Christ's blood shed for atonement and purification
It symbolizes pagan purification rites
It represents the ritual washing of hands
It anticipates the anointing with oil
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's blood shed for atonement and purification
questions.explanation: The sprinkling of blood around the altar in Leviticus prefigures the New Testament theme of Christ's sacrificial blood providing atonement and cleansing (Hebrews 9:12-14).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the burnt offering instructions in Leviticus 1 and emphasizes the importance of offerings without blemish?
options: Exodus 29:38-42
Genesis 1:1-3
Deuteronomy 6:4-5
Psalm 23
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 29:38-42
questions.explanation: Exodus 29:38-42 details offerings of bulls without blemish and parallels Leviticus 1's requirements showing continuity in Israelite sacrificial worship.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is commonly translated as 'sweet savour' in Leviticus 1, and what is its deeper meaning?
options: Reiach (רֵיחַ) meaning a pleasant aroma pleasing to God
Chesed (חֶסֶד) meaning lovingkindness
Shalom (שָׁלוֹם) meaning peace
Elohim (אֱלֹהִים) meaning God
questions.correctAnswer: Reiach (רֵיחַ) meaning a pleasant aroma pleasing to God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'reiach' used in Leviticus 1 describes the burnt offering as a pleasant aroma, symbolizing acceptability and delight to God.

questions.question: Leviticus 1:4 describes the offerer putting his hand on the head of the burnt offering. What is the theological significance of this act?
options: It symbolizes the transfer of sins and identification with the sacrifice
It is a gesture of ownership over the animal
It invokes blessing from the priest
It marks the animal as holy and untouchable
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the transfer of sins and identification with the sacrifice
questions.explanation: Placing the hand on the offering's head symbolized the offerer transferring guilt and identifying with the sacrifice, foundational for atonement theology (Leviticus 1:4).

questions.question: In the context of ancient Near Eastern sacrifices, how does the requirement of an unblemished male animal in Leviticus 1 reflect Israel's covenantal holiness?
options: It emphasizes purity and perfection in offerings to a holy God
It shows flexibility in sacrificial practices
It mimics pagan ritual customs
It indicates economic status of worshippers
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes purity and perfection in offerings to a holy God
questions.explanation: The demand for an unblemished male animal symbolizes the need for holiness and perfection in offerings, reflecting Israel's covenant relationship with a holy God distinct from surrounding cultures (Leviticus 1:3,10).

questions.question: Which New Testament book references the burnt offering as a type for Christ's once-for-all sacrifice, connecting to Leviticus 1?
options: Hebrews
James
Revelation
Acts
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews
questions.explanation: The book of Hebrews extensively references and interprets Levitical sacrifices, including burnt offerings, as types fulfilled in Christ's perfect sacrifice (Hebrews 9:11-14).

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 1, the burnt offering was exclusively a communal sacrifice and could not be brought by individuals.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:2-3 indicates that any individual could bring a burnt offering voluntarily, making it a personal act of worship, not solely communal.

questions.question: Which literary device does Leviticus 1 use by repeatedly ending statements with the phrase 'an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD'?
options: Inclusio, framing the instructions with a repeated phrase
Allegory, telling a hidden meaning
Chiasm, a symmetrical structure
Metaphor, comparing to unrelated things
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the instructions with a repeated phrase
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase acts as an inclusio, a literary device that frames the instructions and emphasizes the theme of pleasing offerings to God (Leviticus 1:9,13,17).

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the requirement that the burnt offering must be 'without blemish' (Leviticus 1:3) primarily teach about God's nature?
options: God is indifferent to the quality of offerings
God demands perfection and holiness in worship
God prefers offerings from the flock over the herd
God accepts any willing offering regardless of condition
questions.correctAnswer: God demands perfection and holiness in worship
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:3 requires a male without blemish for the burnt offering, indicating God's demand for purity and holiness in what is offered to Him. This reflects God's perfect and holy nature requiring a fitting sacrifice (cf. Hebrews 9:14).

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:4, what is the theological significance of the offerer placing his hand upon the head of the burnt offering?
options: It symbolizes the transfer of sin and identification with the sacrifice
It is a ritual act to bless the animal
It signifies the offerer's ownership of the animal
It is a gesture to calm the animal before sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the transfer of sin and identification with the sacrifice
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:4 states the offerer shall put his hand on the head of the burnt offering, which is a symbolic act representing the transfer of guilt and identification with the sacrifice for atonement (cf. Isaiah 53:6; 2 Corinthians 5:21).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about atonement is illustrated by the priests sprinkling the blood around the altar as described in Leviticus 1:5?
options: The blood of animals has no significance
Atonement requires the shedding and application of blood
Atonement is achieved through verbal confession alone
The altar is merely decorative
questions.correctAnswer: Atonement requires the shedding and application of blood
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:5 shows the priests sprinkling the blood of the burnt offering around the altar, teaching the necessity of blood in atonement, symbolizing life given for sin (cf. Hebrews 9:22).

questions.question: In Leviticus 1:6, what does the act of flaying and cutting the burnt offering into pieces teach about the nature of sacrifice?
options: Sacrifices must be partially consumed by the offerer
Sacrifices symbolize the complete dedication and surrender to God
Sacrifices should be given only in large portions
Sacrifices are only symbolic and need no physical preparation
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices symbolize the complete dedication and surrender to God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:6 requires the burnt offering to be flayed and cut into pieces, symbolizing total dedication and surrender of the whole offering to God, prefiguring Christ's complete sacrifice (cf. Romans 12:1).

questions.question: How does Leviticus 1:7 reveal the attribute of God related to divine order and holiness?
options: God is chaotic and accepts disorder
God is indifferent to how sacrifices are prepared
God requires orderly and reverent worship
God demands sacrifices only on mountains
questions.correctAnswer: God requires orderly and reverent worship
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:7 describes priests putting fire and ordering the wood on the altar, reflecting God's attribute of holiness manifested in order and reverence in worship (cf. 1 Corinthians 14:40).

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Leviticus 1:8 and Leviticus 1:9 teach about the burnt offering?
options: The burnt offering is a partial gift to God
The burnt offering is completely consumed by fire as a pleasing aroma to God
The burnt offering is shared between the priests and the offerer
The burnt offering is reserved for feast days only
questions.correctAnswer: The burnt offering is completely consumed by fire as a pleasing aroma to God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:8 and 1:9 together show the priests laying the parts on the fire and burning all as an offering by fire, producing a sweet savor to the LORD, indicating total consumption symbolizing complete consecration and acceptance by God (cf. Ephesians 5:2).

questions.question: What does Leviticus 1:10 teach about the inclusiveness of sacrificial offerings in Israel's worship?
options: Only cattle from the herd could be offered
Offerings could only be grain or fruit
Both sheep and goats of the flock could be offered as burnt sacrifices
Only birds were acceptable offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Both sheep and goats of the flock could be offered as burnt sacrifices
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:10 specifies that burnt sacrifices could be from the flock, including sheep or goats, showing God’s provision for varied acceptable offerings from different animals (cf. Hebrews 10:4).

questions.question: What significance does the direction 'northward' have in the killing of the burnt offering as stated in Leviticus 1:11?
options: It indicates the offering was made secretly
It symbolizes God’s presence and divine order in the sanctuary
It was a random instruction with no meaning
It shows the offerer’s preference
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God’s presence and divine order in the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:11 commands killing the offering on the north side of the altar, reflecting the sacred order and God’s presence in the tabernacle layout, emphasizing reverence and divine appointment (cf. Exodus 26:35).

questions.question: According to Leviticus 1:12, what does the priest’s role in laying the head and fat on the altar fire teach about priestly mediation?
options: The priest serves only as an observer
The priest actively mediates the offerer’s dedication to God
The priest personally consumes the fat
The priest chooses which offerings to accept
questions.correctAnswer: The priest actively mediates the offerer’s dedication to God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:12 shows the priest laying the parts on the altar fire, indicating the priest’s mediatory role presenting the offering before God on behalf of the people (cf. Hebrews 5:1).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is gained by combining Leviticus 1:14 and Leviticus 1:15 regarding the offerings of birds?
options: Bird offerings were optional and symbolic
Bird offerings represented a humble and accessible sacrifice for those unable to provide cattle or sheep
Only pigeons were acceptable offerings
Bird offerings did not involve the priest
questions.correctAnswer: Bird offerings represented a humble and accessible sacrifice for those unable to provide cattle or sheep
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:14–15 describes offerings of turtledoves or young pigeons and the priest’s handling, showing God’s provision for the poor to approach Him through humble sacrifices, emphasizing grace and accessibility (cf. Luke 2:24).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed through His acceptance of burnt offerings 'of a sweet savour' as stated in Leviticus 1:17?
options: God’s wrath alone
God’s delight in worship and atonement
God’s indifference to offerings
God’s partiality to certain animals
questions.correctAnswer: God’s delight in worship and atonement
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:17 says the burnt sacrifice is 'of a sweet savour unto the LORD,' revealing God's delight in worship offered in obedience and His gracious acceptance of atonement (cf. Psalm 51:16-17).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that animal sacrifices in Leviticus 1:1-17 promote superstition and cruelty. What does Leviticus 1:1-17 actually teach about the purpose of these sacrifices?
options: They are meaningless rituals with no spiritual significance
They teach the necessity of atonement and foreshadow Christ’s perfect sacrifice
They encourage violence for personal gain
They are purely cultural traditions with no divine command
questions.correctAnswer: They teach the necessity of atonement and foreshadow Christ’s perfect sacrifice
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:1-17 shows God’s detailed instructions for atoning burnt offerings, symbolizing the seriousness of sin and the need for substitutionary sacrifice, ultimately fulfilled in Christ’s once-for-all sacrifice (cf. Hebrews 10:1-14).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Leviticus 1:4 and Leviticus 1:5 provide about the relationship between the offerer, the sacrifice, and God?
options: The offerer worships independently of the sacrifice
The sacrifice is a symbolic act of atonement with identification and the shedding of blood before God
The offerer performs the sacrifice alone without priestly involvement
The blood is irrelevant to the sacrifice’s acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: The sacrifice is a symbolic act of atonement with identification and the shedding of blood before God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:4 has the offerer lay hands on the offering, signifying identification, and 1:5 requires killing and blood sprinkling by priests, teaching atonement through substitution and blood before God (cf. Romans 3:25).

questions.question: How does Leviticus 1:13 contribute to the understanding of sanctification in the sacrificial system?
options: Sanctification is unrelated to sacrifices
Washing the inwards and legs symbolizes cleansing, reflecting the need for holiness in approach to God
The washing was only for hygiene
Sanctification is purely external and ritualistic
questions.correctAnswer: Washing the inwards and legs symbolizes cleansing, reflecting the need for holiness in approach to God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:13 commands washing the inwards and legs, symbolizing purification and sanctification necessary for acceptable offerings, paralleling the believer’s need for holiness (cf. Psalm 51:7).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Leviticus 1:2 establish in the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It introduces the idea that offerings are unnecessary
It shows God’s covenant relationship initiating worship and atonement practices for Israel
It emphasizes Israel’s independence from God
It rejects the concept of sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s covenant relationship initiating worship and atonement practices for Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 1:2 commands Israel to bring offerings to the LORD, marking the covenantal framework where God institutes worship and atonement, continuing the redemptive narrative from Exodus and pointing forward to Christ (cf. Exodus 19:5-6).
